Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The pattern looks like late 2008: VIX and credit spreads at extremes, equities in deep drawdown, and Treasury yields falling sharply. The policy rate z-score of -1.5 with a 3m change of -3 points to aggressive cuts. Headline CPI is high at +1.0 with a 3m change of +1.0, which fits mid-2008, but the snapshot also shows deflationary pressure setting in.

The unemployment rate z-score is +1.0 with a 12m change of +3, so unemployment is rising fast but is not yet at its peak.

October 2008 fits well on several points. The VIX was extreme, and equities fell sharply in 1m, 3m and 12m terms. Credit spreads were very wide, and the fed funds rate was cut to 1.0% in October. Headline CPI was still elevated, though by October it was falling.

Against that, the 2y yield z-score of -3 and 10y at -2 fit October to November 2008. Gold was up 2.0 over 1m, and in October 2008 gold was roughly flat to down, but in November it rose. Equity 1m returns of -2.5 fit October (-17%), whereas November was -7%, which is also a large drop. The 7-10y Treasury 1m return of +2.0 fits November, when Treasuries rallied. The investment-grade credit 1m return of +2.0 fits November rather than October, when credit fell. Core CPI at +0.5 and headline at +1.0 fit October to November as well. Headline CPI in November had dropped sharply, but the 12m z-score measure is relative to the prior 36 months. The dollar at -1.5 fits too.

I'll go with November 2008.
